prompt: One of eight identical web servers returns 500s for uploads. All eight run the same build.
tells: One of eight identical web servers
why: Same code, one bad host: diff its config, env vars, disk and installed packages against a good one.
trap: A race would hit all eight hosts sometimes, not one host always.

prompt: A payment webhook works in production but times out in staging. Both environments deploy the same container image.
tells: works in production but times out in staging
why: Identical image, different behavior: compare environment variables, secrets, firewall rules and endpoints.
trap: DNS could be the specific culprit, but the move is to diff the two environments to find out.

prompt: After a server was rebuilt from the template, a feature that had worked for months stopped working on it. An engineer recalls hand-editing that server's config last year.
why: The old server had drifted from the template; the rebuild exposed it. Put the setting in version-controlled config.
trap: The rebuild is a change, but the real cause is the undocumented manual edit.

prompt: Nightly reports on one worker show yesterday's date, while every other worker is correct. All workers run the same job code.
why: Likely a different TZ setting on that host: compare system config across workers.
trap: Clock skew means the clock is wrong; here the clock is right but the timezone config differs.

prompt: A new feature works on the developer's laptop but crashes in the container with "undefined API_BASE_URL".
why: The laptop has an environment variable the container was never given.
trap: Same code, different environment; check what each one is configured with.

prompt: Under load, one node pool drops connections while an identical-looking pool doesn't. A comparison shows one has a much smaller connection-tracking table limit set at boot.
why: The table filling up is exhaustion, but the reason only one pool hits it is a drifted kernel setting.
trap: Fix the drift, then fix the limit, or it comes back on the next rebuild.

prompt: An old internal client can reach the API through one load balancer but gets handshake errors through the other. Both were meant to be configured identically.
why: One balancer allows older TLS versions; the "identical" configs aren't.
trap: "Meant to be" is the drift hint; diff the actual settings.

prompt: Only two of ten pods are killed for running out of memory. Their pod spec was copied before the memory limit was raised for the others.
tells: copied before the memory limit was raised
why: Those pods have an old limit; it's a config difference, not a leak.
trap: Out-of-memory kills suggest a leak, but a leak would hit all ten.
